properties.name: Amazon Basin Zone
properties.principle: Hydrology: the land that drains to the Amazon's main stem, from the Andes to the estuary, without the Tocantins. The outline and the Sectors' lines are LBA-ECO CD-06's 33 tributary sub-basins (the Digital Chart of the World's rivers, every land cell given to its nearest river: approximate). Each Sector is a group of whole sub-basins by tributary system; the main stem's own floodplain is cut square to the river at the mouths of the Içá, the Negro and the Xingu. The islands of the Amazon's mouth beyond the source's outlet (eastern Marajó, Caviana, Mexiana, the Bailique group) are added whole from Natural Earth's coast. Framed as climatic because the stories the basin holds are its floods, droughts and fires.

declared.note: The source stops at its outlet (51.42 W, 0.43 S). The islands of the Amazon's mouth beyond it are added whole from Natural Earth's 1:10m coast wherever the source does not already cover them: eastern Marajó (Breves, Soure, Salvaterra, Muaná), Caviana, Mexiana, Jurupari and the Bailique group (13 islands, 25,158 km2). The channels between them are not drawn.

declared.name: Marajó's south shore and the Pará River
declared.note: Marajó's south shore against the Pará River: the Breves channels carry Amazon water into the Pará River, which is the Tocantins' estuary and stays out with the Tocantins, as do its islands and Belém. The line is Natural Earth's coast, approximate. On the north channel's mainland shore, Macapá and Santana lie just outside the source's basin and are not drawn.
